segments.title: Guidance drafted retrospectively to accommodate existing deployments
segments.quote: In practice as a thing that happened which we now have to write guidance about retrospectively.

codes.rationale: Guidance is reactive to deployments already underway, indicating a lack of proactive adaptation.

segments.title: Prioritization driven by crisis, not foresight
segments.quote: The reason it wasn't prioritised is that nothing had gone wrong yet, and our attention is allocated by what has gone wrong.

codes.rationale: Prioritization is reactive to problems, demonstrating a lack of proactive foresight and a deterministic approach.

segments.title: Requirements for system transparency and fallback procedures
segments.quote: A requirement to publish what the system optimises. A requirement for a documented fallback that is tested annually.
segments.full_text: A requirement to publish what the system optimises. A requirement for a documented fallback that is tested annually, because everyone has a fallback on paper and nobody tests it. And a requirement to report performance disaggregated by pedestrian type, which is the one that will get pushed back on hardest because it's the one that would show something.

codes.rationale: The guidance includes requirements for testing and transparency, indicating an attempt to adapt and learn from past experiences.

segments.title: Guidance lacks enforcement power
segments.quote: It’s guidance. Authorities must have regard to it. In practice that means the ones already doing it will cite it and the ones who aren't will note that they’ve had regard to it and carry on.
segments.full_text: It’s guidance. Authorities must have regard to it. In practice that means the ones already doing it will cite it and the ones who aren't will note that they’ve had regard to it and carry on. Making it statutory requires primary legislation and there is no legislative slot.

codes.rationale: The guidance's lack of legal enforceability limits its ability to drive change and represents a lack of substantive responsiveness.

segments.title: Exclusion of key stakeholder groups from drafting
segments.quote: No disability organisations, no residents. I raised it.
segments.full_text: A working group — five authorities, three vendors, two academics. No disability organisations, no residents. I raised it. I was told the timeline didn’t allow for a public consultation, which is true, and also we set the timeline.

codes.rationale: The exclusion of disability organizations and residents from the drafting process demonstrates a closed and exclusive approach to engagement.

summary: This respondent highlights a system where policy development is reactive rather than proactive, driven by crises rather than foresight. The guidance being drafted demonstrates a degree of responsiveness through requirements for testing and transparency, but its lack of enforceability significantly limits its impact. A key theme is the retrospective nature of policy, reacting to existing deployments rather than shaping them. The process of drafting the guidance also reveals a concerning lack of engagement, with crucial stakeholder groups like disability organizations and residents excluded, despite the respondent's objections. This suggests a closed and exclusive approach to policy development, prioritizing expediency over inclusivity.
transcript:
Interview transcript G04 — Policy analyst, national transport ministry
Case: Port Calder adaptive traffic signal and pedestrian detection system  |  SYNTHETIC DATA — not a real interview
[Interviewer] How does central government see deployments like Port Calder's?
[Respondent] As a pilot we can learn from, officially. In practice as a thing that happened which we now have to write guidance about retrospectively. Eleven authorities did something in this space before there was any national position, and the guidance we're now drafting has to be compatible with all eleven, which means it will be weak.
[Interviewer] Could the ministry have moved earlier?
[Respondent] Yes. There was a submission in 2021 recommending exactly that and it wasn't prioritised. I've read it. It's a good submission. The reason it wasn't prioritised is that nothing had gone wrong yet, and our attention is allocated by what has gone wrong. That's the honest mechanism and it's not specific to this file.
[Interviewer] What's going into the guidance?
[Respondent] A requirement to publish what the system optimises. A requirement for a documented fallback that is tested annually, because everyone has a fallback on paper and nobody tests it. And a requirement to report performance disaggregated by pedestrian type, which is the one that will get pushed back on hardest because it's the one that would show something.
[Interviewer] Will it have teeth?
[Respondent] It's guidance. Authorities must have regard to it. In practice that means the ones already doing it will cite it and the ones who aren't will note that they've had regard to it and carry on. Making it statutory requires primary legislation and there is no legislative slot.
[Interviewer] Was anyone outside government involved in drafting?
[Respondent] A working group — five authorities, three vendors, two academics. No disability organisations, no residents. I raised it. I was told the timeline didn't allow for a public consultation, which is true, and also we set the timeline.
